brief.headline: The aluminium curve stopped deepening and settled into a $20 contango while the flat price almost stopped falling and the warehouse draw got ten times bigger - three signs of a market finding a level rather than one breaking down.
bullets: WHAT MOVED, AND HOW LITTLE: on Wednesday's LME official aluminium cash settled $3,240.00 and three-month $3,260.00. Cash fell just $2.00, or 0.06%, after falls of $22.50 and $20.50 on the two preceding sessions. Three consecutive declines, each roughly a tenth of the one before. A market that is still falling but has almost stopped is behaving differently from one that is accelerating lower.

THE CURVE FOUND A LEVEL: the cash-to-three-month contango narrowed to $20.00 from $22.00. Five sessions ago the market was paying a $21.00 premium for immediate metal; it now pays $20.00 to defer it, and that $20.00 has been broadly stable for two rings. A stable contango is a repriced cost of carry, which is an ordinary thing; a widening one would have been a deteriorating market, which is not.

WHY CARRY IS PART OF THE ANSWER BUT NOT ALL OF IT: on the same session the US ten-year Treasury yield printed 5.073%, reported as a nineteen-year high, after US flash PMIs hit multi-year highs and rate expectations moved towards a further increase in October. Higher financing costs push every forward curve towards contango. Yet copper's front did the opposite on the identical ring, widening its premium for immediate metal from $37 to $77 - so the same cost produced opposite outcomes in two metals, and anyone claiming a single clean explanation is overclaiming.

WHAT TO WATCH: warehouse stock drew 750 tonnes to 241,375, a third straight draw and ten times the previous day's, with the week down 2,225 tonnes near multi-decade lows. Against that, three-month settled one dollar below 3,261 - the level that separates this consolidation from a break. One dollar is not a break. Watch today's 13:20 London official for whether that level gives way by a margin that actually means something, and watch whether Chinese demand returns after the 1-8 October holiday or the pre-holiday destocking simply reverses.

lme.commentary: THE THIRD PRE-REGISTERED TEST RESOLVED, AND FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS SEQUENCE IT DID NOT RESOLVE AGAINST THE PAGE - IT RESOLVED INTO THE MIDDLE OPTION. Yesterday this page published three outcomes for today's spread: the contango WIDENS a third time, ending any argument that this is positioning noise; it STABILISES near $20.00, making a new equilibrium the base case; or it NARROWS SHARPLY BACK TOWARDS FLAT, reopening the tightness reading. On the 23-September official cash settled $3,240.00 against three-month $3,260.00: a $20.00 CONTANGO, narrowed by exactly $2.00. THAT IS THE SECOND OPTION, AND IT MATTERS, because a contango that stabilises says something quite different from one that keeps deepening. The seven-session sequence now reads $21.00 backwardation, $18.50, $3.00, minus $10.50, minus $22.00, minus $20.00 - a violent crossing followed by a plateau. THE FLAT PRICE ALSO DECELERATED SHARPLY AND THAT IS THE SECOND REAL FACT OF THE SESSION. Cash fell $2.00 or 0.06% and three-month $4.00 or 0.12%, against falls of $20.50 and $9.00 the session before and $22.50 and $12.00 the session before that. Three consecutive declines, each smaller than the last by roughly an order of magnitude. For the first time in this window three-month fell MORE than cash in dollar terms, which is arithmetically why the contango narrowed rather than widened. THE CROSS-METAL EVIDENCE INVERTED, AND THIS PAGE IS CORRECTING ITSELF IN PUBLIC. Yesterday copper's and zinc's fronts held backwardations while nickel's and lead's contangos tightened, and this page wrote that four of five fronts had moved towards immediacy while aluminium moved away - and leaned on that as evidence of something aluminium-specific. TODAY THE SIGN FLIPPED. Copper's backwardation WIDENED $37.00 to $77.00 and aluminium's contango NARROWED; zinc's backwardation NARROWED $68.00 to $56.00, nickel's contango WIDENED $130.00 to $170.00, lead's WIDENED $26.50 to $42.50. A cross-sectional signal that reverses on consecutive rings is noise in the front, not a regime, and yesterday's framing claimed more than the data could carry. THE HONEST RESIDUAL IS SMALLER AND LESS INTERESTING THAN YESTERDAY'S PAGE IMPLIED: aluminium's front has moved from backwardation to a stable $20.00 contango over five sessions, and no cross-metal control establishes that the cause is aluminium-specific. THE MACRO LEG, BY CONTRAST, GOT UNAMBIGUOUSLY STRONGER AND POINTS THE SAME WAY AS THE CURVE. On this same 23-September session the US ten-year Treasury yield printed 5.073%, described on the public macro board as a NINETEEN-YEAR HIGH, up from the 4.958% this page carried yesterday - roughly eleven basis points in a day, with SMM reporting multiple tenors up nearly twenty basis points and the three-, five-, seven- and ten-year all back above 5%. US flash September purchasing managers' indices were exceptionally strong: manufacturing 57, a fifty-two-month high; services 58.7, a fifty-nine-month high; composite 58.4, the highest since July 2021. Expectations shifted towards a FURTHER Federal Reserve increase in October, with Governor Barr quoted saying more may be needed. A financing cost at a nineteen-year high is a powerful structural argument for a contango and against a backwardation - but copper's front widened its backwardation into exactly that cost on exactly that session, so carry remains a necessary and not a sufficient condition. THE STOCK LINE DID THE MOST WORK IT HAS DONE ALL WEEK. Visible LME stock drew 750 tonnes to 241,375, ten times the previous session's 75 tonnes, a third consecutive draw and a fourth in five sessions, with the week's cumulative draw at 2,225 tonnes or 0.91% as independently reported by SMM. The level sits about 9,840 tonnes below the August mean of 251,215 and close to multi-decade lows. Four of five base-metal stock lines drew on the same ring. THE 3,261 LEVEL WAS BREACHED BY ONE DOLLAR AND THIS PAGE WILL NOT PRETEND THAT IS DECISIVE. Three-month settled $3,260.00, a dollar below the level named in advance as the consolidation-versus-break line. The letter of the pre-registered condition is met; the spirit is not, because a $1.00 margin is indistinguishable from a tick. The test is RE-REGISTERED for today's 13:20 official: a second consecutive settlement below 3,261, and materially below it, is what would earn a change of view.

drivers.text: The exchange curve stopped deepening its contango - a weaker buyer argument than yesterday, but still a buyer argument — On the 23-September LME official cash settled $3,240.00 against three-month $3,260.00, a $20.00 CONTANGO narrowed from $22.00. A market that does not pay a premium for immediate metal is a market in which a buyer can credibly argue against paying a record quarterly premium for guaranteed delivery. The qualification published here is that the front STOPPED deteriorating, which removes the momentum from that argument even as the level itself remains supportive of it.

headlines.title: THE CONTANGO STOPPED DEEPENING AND SETTLED INTO A LEVEL, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT FROM A DETERIORATING FRONT. On the 23-September official cash settled $3,240.00 against three-month $3,260.00, a $20.00 CONTANGO narrowed $2.00 from $22.00. This page published the three-way test in advance for a third time - widen again, stabilise near $20.00, or narrow sharply back towards flat - and it stabilised. The seven-session sequence reads $21.00 backwardation, $18.50, $3.00, minus $10.50, minus $22.00, minus $20.00: a violent crossing followed by a plateau. For the first time in this window three-month fell MORE than cash in dollar terms, which is arithmetically why the contango narrowed.

THE DECLINE ALL BUT STOPPED, AND THE DECELERATION IS ITSELF INFORMATION. Cash fell $2.00 or 0.06% and three-month $4.00 or 0.12%, against $20.50 and $9.00 the previous session and $22.50 and $12.00 the one before. Three consecutive falls, each roughly a tenth of its predecessor. Cash has now fallen on five of the last six settled sessions but sits only $9.63 below the August monthly mean of $3,249.63. A market still drifting lower at a hundredth of last week's pace is consolidating, not breaking.

THE 3,261 LEVEL BROKE BY ONE DOLLAR - THE LETTER OF THE TEST, NOT THE SPIRIT. Three-month settled $3,260.00, the first settlement below 3,261 since 15-September and a dollar under this page's pre-registered consolidation-versus-break line. THE PAGE PUBLISHES THE BREACH AND EXPLICITLY DECLINES TO TREAT IT AS DECISIVE: a $1.00 margin is inside any honest definition of noise, and declaring a breakdown on it would be the kind of over-reading this page criticises elsewhere. The condition is re-registered: a SECOND consecutive settlement below 3,261, and materially below it, is what earns a change of view.

THE STOCK DRAW GOT TEN TIMES BIGGER AND IS NOW A SIGNAL RATHER THAN A ROUNDING. Visible LME stock drew 750 tonnes to 241,375 - a third consecutive draw, a fourth in five sessions, against 75 tonnes the session before. SMM independently records the identical 750-tonne fall and puts the week's cumulative draw at 2,225 tonnes, or 0.91%. The level is about 9,840 tonnes below the August mean of 251,215 and close to multi-decade lows. Four of the five base-metal stock lines drew on the same ring - lead 3,775 tonnes, copper 1,750, nickel 30 - with only zinc building, by 150.

US flash September purchasing managers' indices hit multi-year highs - manufacturing 57, a fifty-two-month high; services 58.7, a fifty-nine-month high; composite 58.4, the highest since July 2021 - and expectations moved towards a FURTHER Federal Reserve increase in October, with Governor Barr reported saying more may be needed and multiple tenors up nearly twenty basis points. The dollar index rose 0.42% to 101.025 and the LME euro fixing weakened to 1.14120 from 1.14630. A financing cost at a nineteen-year high is the strongest structural argument yet carried here FOR a contango.

THE CROSS-METAL SIGNAL REVERSED ITS SIGN IN ONE SESSION, AND THIS PAGE IS CORRECTING ITSELF IN PUBLIC. Yesterday copper's and zinc's backwardations held while nickel's and lead's contangos tightened, and this page called that four-of-five moving towards immediacy against aluminium alone. TODAY IT INVERTED: copper's backwardation WIDENED $37.00 to $77.00 and aluminium's contango NARROWED, while zinc's backwardation narrowed $68.00 to $56.00, nickel's contango widened $130.00 to $170.00 and lead's widened $26.50 to $42.50. A cross-sectional signal that flips on consecutive rings is noise in the front, not a regime. Yesterday's framing claimed more than the data supports and the claim is withdrawn.

THE CENTRAL CHINA PHYSICAL DISCOUNT PERSISTED AND THE STATED REASON IS DEMAND, NOT LOGISTICS. SMM's 24-September minutes record central China transactions settling at a DISCOUNT of 50-80 yuan/mt against the SHFE October contract, with high aluminium prices and insufficient peak-season strength limiting downstream buying and market trading described as sluggish. SMM A00 spot premiums stood at 10-30 yuan/mt and SMM A00 closed 24,240 yuan/mt, down a further 30 yuan/mt. The confirming number is the one this page has tracked throughout: the liquid-aluminium share fell a further 0.02 percentage points on select downstream production cuts.

CHINESE DESTOCKING ACCELERATED TO THE LARGEST FIGURE THIS PAGE HAS CARRIED - AND THE NAMED DRIVERS BOTH REVERSE. SMM reports social inventory of aluminium ingots down 43,000 tonnes from Monday and 55,000 tonnes from last Monday, with the three-region total down 12,500 tonnes, and attributes the widening draw to disrupted Xinjiang outbound shipments combined with downstream stockpiling ahead of the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays. A rail disruption and pre-holiday stocking are both temporary by construction. South China saw significant destocking with large buyers raising purchase prices to make markets, but SMM notes spot circulation loosened quickly from a tight state as shipments increased.

ALUMINIUM BAHRAIN'S RECOVERY WAS CORROBORATED A FOURTH TIME IN EIGHT DAYS. SMM's 24-September minutes record Alba's operating capacity recovered to around 1.3 million tonnes, citing foreign media reports, and frame it as further lifting operating capacity outside China. Against a pre-war plant of about 1,623 kt that is roughly 80%. A figure that survives four separate public retellings without revision is materially stronger evidence than a single report - though it still sits against CRU Group being reported as holding that Gulf production is down around 25% year on year, and this page will not quietly pick the one that fits its narrative.

THE RESTART PACE IS GUIDED TO SLOW, WHICH IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE SUPPLY STORY. SMM's comprehensive outlook states that production resumptions in the Middle East continued to ACCELERATE but that some new projects were DELAYED, and that the pace of operating-capacity increases is expected to SLOW in the coming months. The biggest single tranche is already in the market; less follows behind it than the restart list implies. This is the clearest published counterweight to the restart-driven bear case and it is dated.

BRENT SNAPPED A FIVE-SESSION LOSING STREAK AND THE COST FLOOR STOPPED FALLING. Brent rose 2.41% to about $101.64 on the 23-September reference session, reclaiming the $100 handle on geopolitical risk, with European gas TTF also up about 1.34% to EUR 72.87 from the 71.91 carried yesterday. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT CUTS AGAINST THE OBVIOUS ONE: a falling cost floor lowers marginal-cost support under the price, so a complex that has stopped falling and started rising is mildly SUPPORTIVE of price rather than bearish. It is also mildly adverse for the two gas-exposed assets named on this page and for Slovalco's restart economics.

DRY BULK FREIGHT REFRESHED ON A NEWER MARK AND IT IS MATERIALLY HIGHER THAN THE FIGURE THIS PAGE HAS BEEN CARRYING. The Baltic Dry Index closed 3,430 on 23-September, down 0.06% on the day but near its highest since 14-September and UP 19.01% over the past month and 53.13% year on year - against the 3,157 mark this page had carried for several runs. Capesize fell 0.5% to 5,861; panamax rose 1.5% to 2,333; supramax rose 0.1% to 1,778. Higher bulk freight raises the delivered cost of bauxite and alumina into refineries and smelters, which supports the cost floor while penalising long-haul trade.

THE SECTION 232 HEADLINE RATE IS RE-VERIFIED AND UNCHANGED AT 50% ON ARTICLES AND 25% ON DERIVATIVES, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU. No new instrument printed in the last 48 hours. At the 23-September cash settlement of $3,240.00 the 50% leg alone is about $1,620.00/t, down $1.00/t on the session PURELY because the exchange price fell - the tariff leg is mechanical arithmetic on the exchange price, not a change in physical tightness, and this page decomposes it every run so a reader can see which part of a US delivered price is policy and which is market. Next dated step: a US vehicle and dairy import ban on 29-SEPTEMBER.

METLEN WAS REPORTED INVESTING EUR 25 MILLION IN A GREEK RECYCLED-ALUMINIUM PLANT, boosting scrap processing and downstream integration. Recorded because secondary-capacity investment accumulates into a structural substitution signal against primary demand growth, and weighted as SMALL because a single plant-scale project does not move a global balance and no public tonnage this page can verify was attached to the report. The context is a European scrap market where compliant material is scarce: SMM notes tax-invoice enforcement in central China is tightening compliant scrap supply and that the A00-to-scrap spread in Foshan stood around 2,512 yuan/mt for mixed extrusion scrap free of paint on 22-September.

CHINA'S CAST ALUMINIUM ALLOY INGOT INVENTORY FELL 2,700 TONNES WEEK ON WEEK TO 31,800 TONNES, ENDING A SIX-WEEK BUILD. SMM attributes the shift to a widening spot-futures spread and the release of pre-holiday stockpiling demand, and explicitly warns that whether demand can be SUSTAINED AFTER THE HOLIDAY still warrants attention. SMM ADC12 held at 24,500 yuan/mt, with cost support described as strong because stricter tax-invoice enforcement is raising compliant raw-material procurement costs - a cost-push resilience story rather than a demand-pull one, and the distinction matters.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

NALCO IS THE MOST FULLY INTEGRATED PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL - IT MINES ITS OWN BAUXITE, REFINES ITS OWN ALUMINA AND SMELTS - AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THIS PRINT IS USEFUL RATHER THAN JUST GOOD. earnings.note: BACKFILLED INTO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A FULL FOUR-QUARTER SOURCED HISTORY. Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

earnings.note: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL - THE FOURTH READING OF THE SAME PRE-REGISTERED TEST, AND STILL THE SINGLE MOST INFORMATIVE SCHEDULED EVENT ON THIS PAGE. The contango crossed, more than doubled, and has now PLATEAUED: $3.00 backwardation, minus $10.50, minus $22.00, minus $20.00. THE QUESTION IS STATED IN ADVANCE AGAIN: does the contango CONFIRM the plateau by settling between $15.00 and $25.00, which would make a new equilibrium the base case and close this line of enquiry; does it RESUME WIDENING beyond $25.00, which would reopen the deterioration reading; or does it NARROW BELOW $10.00, which would put a return to backwardation back in play within days? The published reversal condition is unchanged: a return to BACKWARDATION BEYOND $15.00 on a settled official restores the bull case towards 25%. Watch the stock line with equal attention - a fourth consecutive draw alongside a stable front would be the first genuinely coherent pair of readings in two weeks.

THE 3,261 LEVEL WAS BREACHED BY ONE DOLLAR AND THE TEST IS RE-REGISTERED RATHER THAN CLOSED. Three-month settled $3,260.00 on Wednesday, a dollar below the level this page named in advance as the consolidation-versus-break line and the first settlement beneath it since 15-September. A $1.00 margin is inside any honest definition of noise, so the bear case is raised by only two points and the condition is restated: a SECOND consecutive settlement below 3,261, and materially below it, is what would earn a further change of view. SMM's suggested core range for LME aluminium is $3,220-3,300, a band whose floor sits $40.00 below the level, which is itself informative about how the market is framing the downside. On the weekly Elliott count the level sits close to where the position-degree structure turns.

THE NEXT FEDERAL OPEN MARKET COMMITTEE MEETING, AND ITS RELEVANCE IS NOW THE HIGHEST IT HAS BEEN ON THIS PAGE. The US ten-year printed a NINETEEN-YEAR HIGH of 5.073% on 23-September and US flash September PMIs hit multi-year highs - manufacturing 57, services 58.7, composite 58.4 - with SMM reporting expectations for an October increase INTENSIFYING and Governor Barr saying further increases may be needed. With the dot plot at a 4.1% median for 2026 and two meetings left, the projections imply at least one further rise before year-end. Carry acts on the CURVE rather than the flat price, and the curve is where this page's central question sits: a further increase argues against the contango reversing; a HOLD would remove the cleanest structural argument against a return to backwardation. THE QUALIFICATION THAT SURVIVES: copper widened its backwardation into this same cost on this same session.

THE NEXT DATED STEP IN THE US-CANADA TARIFF SCHEDULE, NOW FIVE DAYS OUT: a US vehicle and dairy import ban takes effect, following Canada's 50% counter-tariffs across CAD 27.6bn in force since 08-September and the 08-September White House annex that lifted previously exempt downstream aluminium lines to a combined levy of up to 100%. THE CONTEXT THAT MAKES THIS DATE INTERESTING IS UNCHANGED AND UNRETRACTED: on 22-September Novelis was reported cutting production and about 80 jobs at Kingston, Ontario explicitly on Section 232 costs - the first clearly attributed capacity consequence of this cycle, arriving a week before the next escalation. At the 23-September cash settlement of $3,240.00 the 50% leg alone is about $1,620.00/t.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE QUARTERLY PREMIUM SETTLEMENT - STILL THE LARGEST SINGLE DATED EVENT LEFT ON THIS PAGE AND NOW INSIDE TWO WEEKS. The pending range carried here is $280-310/t against a settled Q3 record of $395/t, a fall of 22-29% if it lands inside; it is unchanged for a NINTH consecutive run because no newer dated evidence has printed. THE BUYER'S CASE STOPPED STRENGTHENING THIS RUN AND THIS PAGE SAYS SO: the exchange curve narrowed its contango $2.00 to $20.00 rather than deepening further, and the cross-metal pattern that reinforced the argument yesterday inverted. Alongside it sit producer offers of $310-325/t, Alba corroborated a FOURTH time at about 1.3 Mt, softer European premiums, and a central-China spot market transacting at a 50-80 yuan/mt discount to the October contract.

CHINA'S NATIONAL DAY HOLIDAY AND THE POST-HOLIDAY REBUILD TEST - THE CLEANEST FORWARD EXPERIMENT AVAILABLE ON CHINESE DEMAND, AND THE STAKES ROSE THIS RUN. SMM attributes the current destocking - now 43,000 tonnes from Monday and 55,000 tonnes from last Monday, with the three regions down 12,500 tonnes and cast alloy ingot inventory down 2,700 tonnes ending a six-week build - to a Xinjiang outbound shipment disruption and pre-holiday stockpiling, BOTH OF WHICH REVERSE BY DESIGN. The larger the pre-holiday draw, the larger the potential post-holiday rebuild. The test is explicit: STRONG post-holiday operating rates that absorb the returning metal would mean the tightness was genuine; a MUTED return with inventory rebuilding would confirm it was seasonal and logistics-driven. The leading indicators point to the muted outcome - a central-China spot discount of 50-80 yuan/mt, a liquid-aluminium share down a further 0.02 percentage points, and SMM describing the cast-alloy September peak season as less robust than expected. Note the one-to-two-week reporting lag on operating-rate surveys.

THE MONTHLY CARBON-INPUT SETTLEMENT CYCLE IS OPEN, OVERDUE AND HAS STILL NOT PRINTED - A SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE RUN. Prebaked anode, coal tar pitch and green petcoke marks normally settle around the 17th-18th of each month. THE DIRECTIONAL SIGNPOST REVERSED THIS RUN AND THAT IS THE NEWS: Brent SNAPPED a five-session losing streak, rising 2.41% back above $101, and European gas rose about 1.34%. The case for a sharply LOWER settlement is now the weakest it has been this week. This page will append a mark to the input histories only when a dated public figure exists.

THE TIMETABLE IS WHY THIS IS NOT PRICED AS IMMINENT: a post-November US timetable places any agreement outside this quarter, and Iran's conditions are maximalist. Nothing operational has changed on the water, and Brent's 2.41% rise on 23-September was publicly attributed to geopolitical RISK rather than relief.

FOR THIS MARKET: regional delivered prices are currently set by tariff policy rather than physical scarcity, so any movement on the trade file transmits directly into the premium complex. The meeting happening is not the same as an outcome being published.

risks.text: THE CONTANGO STABILISED INSTEAD OF DEEPENING AND THE TREND IS CUT FROM UP TO FLAT - THE FIRST DOWNGRADE OF THIS ARROW IN THIS CYCLE, AND IT IS EARNED. The seven-run sequence is $21.00 backwardation, $18.50, $3.00, minus $10.50, minus $22.00, minus $20.00. The third pre-registered three-way test resolved into the MIDDLE option: the contango narrowed $2.00 rather than widening a third time. A front that has plateaued is not a front that is deteriorating, and holding the arrow at UP would be reading momentum into a flat line. THE CROSS-METAL EVIDENCE THAT THIS PAGE LEANED ON YESTERDAY INVERTED AND THE CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN: copper's backwardation WIDENED $37.00 to $77.00 while aluminium's contango narrowed, and zinc, nickel and lead all moved the other way from where they moved yesterday. A cross-sectional signal that flips sign on consecutive rings is noise, and yesterday's page treated it as structure. WHY NOT DOWN: one plateau session does not reverse a $41.00 move, and the published reversal condition - a return to BACKWARDATION BEYOND $15.00 on a settled official - is still unmet. Today's 13:20 London official is the fourth reading.

THE FEDERAL RESERVE PATH AND THE FINANCING COST ARE RAISED FROM FLAT TO UP, AND THIS IS THE BIGGEST SINGLE CHANGE ON THE REGISTER TODAY. The US ten-year Treasury yield printed 5.073% on the 23-September reference session, reported as a NINETEEN-YEAR HIGH, up about eleven basis points from the 4.958% carried yesterday; SMM records multiple tenors up nearly twenty basis points with the three-, five-, seven- and ten-year all back above 5%. US flash September PMIs printed multi-year highs - manufacturing 57 (fifty-two-month high), services 58.7 (fifty-nine-month high), composite 58.4 (highest since July 2021) - and expectations moved towards a FURTHER increase in October, with Governor Barr reported saying more may be needed. The Committee already raised 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16-September, unanimously at 12-0, lifting its median 2026 projection to 4.1% from 3.8% in June. YESTERDAY THIS PAGE CUT THIS ARROW TO FLAT BECAUSE THE CROSS-METAL BOARD CONTRADICTED THE CARRY STORY; TODAY THE CROSS-METAL BOARD REVERSED ITSELF, SO THE CONTRADICTION WAS NOISE AND THE DOWNGRADE WAS AN OVERREACTION. Raising the arrow back to UP is the honest response. THE DISCIPLINE THAT SURVIVES: copper widened its backwardation into this same cost on this same ring, so carry is a direction of pressure, not a determinant.

TARIFF POLICY REMAINS THE DOMINANT SETTER OF REGIONAL PRICE AND THE TREND IS CUT FROM UP TO FLAT BECAUSE NO NEW INSTRUMENT AND NO NEW ATTRIBUTED CONSEQUENCE PRINTED IN THE LAST 48 HOURS. THE ARITHMETIC IS RESTATED EVERY RUN SO A READER CAN SEPARATE POLICY FROM MARKET: at the 23-September cash settlement of $3,240.00 the 50% leg alone is about $1,620.00/t, down $1.00/t on the session PURELY because the exchange price fell. Visible LME stock fell 750 tonnes to 241,375 on the 23-September session, against 75 tonnes the session before - a third consecutive draw and a fourth in five sessions. SMM independently records the identical 750-tonne fall and puts the week's cumulative draw at 2,225 tonnes, or 0.91%. The level is about 9,840 tonnes below the August mean of 251,215 and close to multi-decade lows. Four of five base-metal stock lines drew on the same ring - lead 3,775 tonnes, copper 1,750, nickel 30 - with only zinc building by 150. SMM's 24-September minutes corroborate for a FOURTH time in eight days that Aluminium Bahrain's operating capacity recovered to around 1.3 million tonnes, citing foreign media reports, and explicitly frame it as further lifting operating capacity outside China; against a pre-war plant of about 1,623 kt that is roughly 80%. AGAINST IT, CRU GROUP IS REPORTED AS HOLDING THAT GULF PRODUCTION IS DOWN AROUND 25% YEAR ON YEAR, and a public reference board still carries GCC production down 44% year on year in July. Both cannot be fully right and this page will not quietly pick the one that fits its narrative; a figure that survives four separate public retellings without revision is nonetheless stronger evidence than a single report. WHY THE ARROW STAYS DOWN: SMM continues to guide that while resumptions ACCELERATED, SOME NEW PROJECTS WERE DELAYED and the pace of operating-capacity increases outside China is expected to SLOW in the coming months. The published deficit spread of 300,000-500,000 tonnes base against up to 1.4 million tonnes bull remains the honest encoding of the disagreement.

THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM OVERHANG IS HELD AT UP, AND THE EVIDENCE REMAINS A PRICE RATHER THAN AN INVENTORY. Central China transactions on 23-September settled at a DISCOUNT of 50-80 yuan/mt against the SHFE October contract, with SMM recording that high aluminium prices and insufficient peak-season strength limited buying sentiment among downstream processing enterprises and left market trading sluggish. A physical market transacting at a discount to its own futures because buyers will not step up is a demand statement, not a logistics one. THE CONFIRMING NUMBER IS THE ONE THIS PAGE HAS TRACKED THROUGHOUT: the liquid-aluminium share FELL a further 0.02 percentage points on select downstream curtailments, and SMM describes the cast aluminium alloy 'September peak season' as LESS ROBUST THAN EXPECTED with end-user orders improved only slightly from the off-season. The settled Q3 benchmark of $395/t is not stale, because a quarterly benchmark is fixed until the quarter turns, but it is increasingly disconnected. THE PENDING RANGE HERE IS $280-310/t, a fall of 22-29%, unchanged for a NINTH consecutive run because no newer dated evidence has printed. WHAT CHANGED: the buyer's case of the last two runs rested on a contango that was DEEPENING while other metals moved towards immediacy; on the 23-September official it narrowed $2.00 to $20.00 and the cross-metal pattern inverted. A stable $20.00 contango is still a buyer's argument - the market does not value immediacy - but it is a weaker one than a front in visible deterioration, and flat is the honest arrow.

STRAIT OF HORMUZ AND REGIONAL SHIPPING DISRUPTION IS HELD AT FLAT, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE DE-ESCALATION SIGNAL OF TWO RUNS AGO PRODUCED NOTHING OPERATIONAL IN THE LAST 48 HOURS. The dated position is unchanged: Trump reiterated on 22-September at the UN General Assembly that the United States would reach an agreement with Iran AFTER the November midterm elections; Araghchi met Witkoff in New York with a three-hour meeting described as very productive and another to be arranged; Iran publicly set maximalist conditions for reopening the Strait - lifting the maritime blockade, unfreezing all Iranian assets, ending the war on all regional fronts. NOTHING HAS CHANGED ON THE WATER. The prior evidence stands unrefuted: Reuters tracking cited 20-September put daily commodity transits at 3-6 ships between 2 and 18 September against a normal ten-day average of 12-18, and a tanker was reportedly struck near Khasab, Oman on 18-September with attribution still UNCONFIRMED. WHAT IS NEW AND CUTS THE OTHER WAY: Brent rose 2.41% on 23-September with the public board attributing the bounce to GEOPOLITICAL RISK - a price signal pointing towards escalation rather than resolution, though an oil-market attribution is weak evidence about a specific waterway. TREAT THESE AS REPORTED DIPLOMATIC STATEMENTS AND MARKET ATTRIBUTIONS, NOT SETTLED OUTCOMES.

THE EX-CHINA RESTART PIPELINE IS VISIBLE AND DATED BUT THE TREND IS HELD AT FLAT, BECAUSE IT KEEPS GETTING SLOWER AND LARGER AT THE SAME TIME. The publicly reported list carries Aluminium Bahrain at about 1.3 Mt annualised against a 1,623 kt plant, now corroborated by a FOURTH source in eight days; Century's Mt Holly at full capacity for the first time since 2015 on a $50m investment restarting more than 50,000 t; Slovalco restarting the first 75,000 t of 175,000 t guided for Q4-2026, with its power input having moved mildly ADVERSELY this run as European gas rose about 1.34%; Magnitude 7 Metals with a first potline guided before end-2026 for about 75,000 t, publicly attributed to the 50% US tariff; and EGA's DX+ Ultra licence to NALCO for a proposed 500,000 t/y Angul expansion. AGAINST THAT, SMM CONTINUES TO GUIDE THAT SOME NEW PROJECTS WERE DELAYED AND THE PACE OF OPERATING-CAPACITY INCREASES WILL SLOW IN COMING MONTHS - and separately, US Section 232 has begun REMOVING North American conversion capacity, with Novelis cutting production at Kingston, Ontario. ADDED THIS RUN ON THE SECONDARY SIDE: METLEN was reported on 23-September investing EUR 25 million in a Greek recycled-aluminium plant, recorded because secondary capacity accumulates as a structural substitute for primary demand growth, and weighted as small. Restarts are slow, none of this lands this quarter, and the evidence points in opposite directions. Flat is the honest arrow.

EU CARBON-BORDER COST IS A SLOW, STRUCTURAL RISK TO EUROPEAN DELIVERED PRICE AND IT IS HELD AT FLAT. SMM analysis published 22-September, using Eurostat Comext data updated 15-September, shows extra-EU aluminium foil imports (HS7607) at 137.28 kt in January-July 2026, DOWN 22.2% year on year, with theoretical net certificate exposure for identified non-exempt origins down 24.1% to 326.74 kt CO2e. YET TRADE-WEIGHTED UNIT EXPOSURE ROSE 0.7%, from 2.6377 to 2.6550 t CO2e per tonne, because the origin mix shifted: China and Turkiye together now account for 75.8% of calculable exposure against 69.7% a year earlier, and China's default net unit exposure of 4.5559 t CO2e/t is about 2.5 times Turkiye's 1.8191. WHY IT IS FLAT RATHER THAN UP: the mechanism is known, the parameters are published, and nothing accelerated in the last 48 hours - aluminium carries a 10% mark-up in 2026 against a 97.5% CBAM factor, and certificate prices are EUR 75.36 for Q1 and EUR 75.28 for Q2 with Q3 unpublished as of 18-September. THE USEFUL WARNING IS METHODOLOGICAL: falling import volumes do not establish that unit carbon-cost exposure has eased, and a 'low-carbon' label is not a substitute for installation-level verified data.

THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
